pages.title: Packing guide
pages.heading: Pack with the whole journey in mind.
pages.intro: A shipment can pass through several vehicles and handling points. Prepare the outer packaging, inner protection and labels as one system—not as an afterthought.

sections.title: Choose packaging for the contents
paragraphs: Start with the packed weight, shape and fragility of the goods. Use a sound outer container with enough strength for the load and room for protective material. Reused packaging should be clean, dry and free of damage; remove obsolete labels and barcodes.

A decorative retail box is not necessarily a transport container. Fragile or unusually shaped goods may need a second protective outer box or specialist packaging. Ask your shipping contact about the planned handling method before sealing a heavy or awkward item.

sections.title: Prevent movement inside the package
items: Wrap separate items individually and protect corners, edges and exposed surfaces.
Fill empty spaces with suitable cushioning so the contents do not move freely.
Keep fragile items separated from one another and from the outer walls.
Protect documents from moisture and bending using suitable inner protection.
Do not rely on a fragile label to compensate for inadequate packaging.

sections.title: Seal, label and measure the finished package
paragraphs: Close the container with a sealing method appropriate to its material and weight. Place the final shipping label on a clear, accessible surface rather than across an edge or an opening. Keep addresses and barcodes legible, and follow the agreed instructions for attaching customs paperwork.

Weigh and measure after packing. Record the longest outside dimensions, including protrusions, and count every package. Keep a photograph of the prepared goods and packaging for your records; a photograph does not establish carrier acceptance or insurance coverage.

sections.title: Pallets, liquids and specialist cargo
paragraphs: Palletised loads need a stable base and securing suitable for the planned transport. Avoid unsupported overhang and tell operations whether lifting equipment is needed at either end. Crates, bands and wrapping must suit the actual cargo rather than simply its appearance.

Liquids, batteries, chemicals, perishables and temperature-sensitive products need an acceptance review before packing arrangements are finalised. Some goods cannot travel on the proposed route. Do not improvise dangerous-goods packaging or hide regulated contents.

pages.title: International shipping
pages.kicker: PREPARE FOR THE BORDER, NOT JUST THE DISTANCE
pages.heading: A clearer start to an international journey.
pages.intro: Cross-border shipping adds documentation, import requirements and responsibilities to the physical movement of goods. Confirm those details before collection rather than when the shipment reaches customs.

sections.title: Check the item and the destination first
paragraphs: Describe what the goods are, what they are made from and how they will be used. Identify the destination country and the intended recipient. An item that can move domestically may be restricted, licensed or prohibited on an international route.

Ask your shipping contact to review the proposed movement, transport mode and any partner-carrier requirements. Route availability, cargo acceptance, broker arrangements and delivery conditions must be confirmed for the particular shipment; a website guide is not an acceptance decision.

sections.title: Prepare information that agrees across documents
items: Full sender and recipient names, usable contact details and complete addresses.
Specific item descriptions, quantities, declared values and currency.
Country of manufacture or production, which may differ from the dispatch country.
Packed weights, dimensions and the number of packages.
Commercial invoice or other supporting documents as required for the transaction.
Any applicable permits, certificates, importer details or broker instructions, confirmed for the destination.

sections.title: Agree who handles customs and charges
paragraphs: Clarify the importer’s responsibilities, the intended broker where applicable, and who is expected to pay transport charges, duties, taxes and clearance-related fees. Do not assume that a transport quotation includes every destination charge.

Recipients may need to provide information or authorise a clearance step. Keep a reliable contact available while the shipment moves. A complete document pack helps preparation, but it does not guarantee customs release or a delivery date.

sections.title: Follow the approved journey
paragraphs: After booking is confirmed, retain the Relay reference and share the private tracking link only with the intended recipients. Relay tracking shows milestones published by operations, not a continuous GPS signal.

If a partner such as FedEx is confirmed for a shipment, ask for the applicable carrier reference and service details. Partner rules apply to that confirmed service. Relay does not currently provide automatic FedEx tracking synchronisation, and this guide is not a claim of FedEx affiliation or universal carrier coverage.

pages.title: Customs and documents
pages.heading: Get the paperwork ready for review.
pages.intro: Customs requirements depend on the goods, the transaction and the countries involved. Use this guide to prepare questions and information—not as a substitute for destination-specific advice.

sections.title: Describe the goods, not just the parcel
paragraphs: Descriptions such as “parts,” “gift” or “samples” may not tell a reviewer what is actually inside. Identify each kind of item separately, its material or composition, its intended use and the quantity. Make sure the description agrees with the goods and the other documents.

Provide an accurate value and currency even when the recipient is not paying for the item. Do not deliberately undervalue goods or use a gift description to disguise a commercial transaction. Ask operations which valuation evidence and invoice format apply.

sections.title: A practical document preparation list
items: Commercial invoice or other appropriate transaction document, where required.
Packing information showing package count, item quantities and relevant weights.
Sender, recipient and importer contact details, with identifiers where required.
Country-of-origin information and any applicable supporting evidence.
Product classification information or HS code for review by the responsible party; do not guess a classification.
Permits, licences or product certificates when the goods and destination require them.
Broker contact information and agreed clearance instructions where applicable.

sections.title: Understand the roles before dispatch
paragraphs: The shipper is responsible for supplying truthful information about the goods. The importer or recipient may have local obligations and may need to answer questions, provide documents or make a payment. Confirm the responsible parties and any broker arrangements with your shipping contact.

Duties, taxes, inspections and release decisions are determined by the relevant authorities and applicable rules. This website does not calculate official customs assessments, file declarations or promise clearance on your behalf.

sections.title: When a shipment is awaiting clearance
paragraphs: Keep the tracking reference and any document request together. Respond to your known shipping contact with the requested information through an agreed channel. Do not place identity documents, account credentials or sensitive records in a public quote form.

A customs milestone does not by itself identify the cause of a delay or the amount due. Check the published note and ask operations for clarification. If Relay publishes a manual payment request, verify the instructions with your known contact before transferring funds.

pages.title: Understanding shipping costs
pages.kicker: KNOW WHAT GOES INTO A QUOTE
pages.heading: Better details. A more useful quotation.
pages.intro: Price depends on the journey and the packed cargo—not weight alone. Understand the information that supports a quote, then ask operations to confirm the actual service and charges.

sections.title: The details that affect a quotation
items: Origin and destination, including the relevant collection and delivery locations.
Transport mode, requested timing and the availability of the proposed route.
Number of packages, packed weight and outside dimensions for each piece.
Cargo type, special handling needs, access conditions and lifting requirements.
Any applicable fuel, remote-area, oversized-piece or other service-specific surcharges.
Customs, taxes, destination handling and other charges that may be separate from transport.

sections.title: Actual weight and volume-based weight
paragraphs: A large lightweight package can occupy more vehicle space than its scale weight suggests. Some services compare actual weight with a dimensional or volume-based weight when assessing charges. The calculation factor, rounding, minimums and applicability depend on the specific service.

Measure the finished package rather than the item before packing. Ask your shipping contact which divisor and charging rules apply. The planner below is arithmetic only: it does not select a carrier tariff, calculate a price or confirm how Relay will bill a shipment.

sections.title: Check what is included—and what is not
paragraphs: Before accepting arrangements, ask whether the stated amount covers collection, transport, delivery and any expected handling. Confirm currency, validity, exclusions and how changes in the declared size or weight will be handled.

A quote enquiry is not a confirmed price, booking, invoice or payment request. Any manual payment instructions shown on a tracking page are a separate operations workflow; a customer’s transfer reference still requires administrator verification.

sections.title: Send useful details from the start
paragraphs: Use the quote form for your route, mode, general cargo type and total weight. Put package count, individual dimensions, ready date and handling requirements in the notes. For sensitive documentation, ask your shipping contact for the appropriate private channel.

There is no instant rate engine on this website. Operations reviews the request before sharing availability and pricing. Do not interpret the planner or an estimated arrival shown in tracking as a guaranteed rate or transit commitment.

pages.title: Restricted items and acceptance
pages.kicker: CHECK FIRST. NEVER DISGUISE THE CONTENTS.
pages.heading: Not everything can travel on every route.
pages.intro: Acceptance can change with the item, its quantity, the transport mode, the carrier and the destination. Check potentially regulated goods with operations before collection or payment.

sections.title: Items that need particular care before booking
items: Batteries and equipment containing batteries, including power banks.
Perfumes, aerosols, paints, fuels, solvents and other potentially flammable products.
Chemicals, compressed gases, dry ice and goods with dangerous-goods classifications.
Medicines, medical products, food, plants, seeds and other regulated biological goods.
Perishables or goods that require a controlled temperature.
High-value articles, cash-like items, weapons-related goods or other specially controlled products.

sections.title: This is a prompt to ask—not a permitted-items list
paragraphs: The examples above are not exhaustive and do not mean that Relay accepts those goods. Some may be prohibited outright; others may require a specialist service, documentation, approved packaging or a qualified shipper. An item not listed here may still be restricted.

Do not bring regulated goods to a collection point or pack them into a general parcel without written acceptance for the proposed movement. Do not remove hazard markings or use a vague description to bypass a review.

sections.title: Information to share with operations
paragraphs: Provide the product’s correct identity, intended use, quantity and packaging details. Where relevant, be ready to supply manufacturer information, a safety data sheet, battery specifications or required certificates through an agreed private channel.
A manufacturer’s product name alone may not be enough to assess the transport classification. Ask which information is needed before buying packaging or committing to a delivery date.

sections.title: Acceptance must be specific
paragraphs: Ask whether the exact goods are accepted on the intended land, sea, air or combined route and whether any origin, transit or destination restrictions apply. Do not assume that a partner’s general website policy confirms a Relay booking.
For regulated cargo, seek qualified guidance and follow the applicable laws and carrier requirements. This guide does not provide instructions for preparing or declaring dangerous goods.

pages.title: Business shipping preparation
pages.kicker: MAKE THE NEXT HANDOVER A CLEARER ONE
pages.heading: Build a more consistent shipping routine.
pages.intro: Whether you send customer orders or occasional business cargo, clear shipment information helps operations assess the right next step. Start with a repeatable preparation process.

sections.title: Prepare a useful shipping profile
items: Common origin and destination routes, with any access restrictions.
Typical package counts, packed dimensions, weights and product categories.
Expected frequency, ready dates and delivery priorities.
Any fragile, regulated, valuable or temperature-sensitive items requiring review.
The people responsible for cargo readiness, documents and recipient communication.
The quotation, payment and reporting information your team needs to review.

sections.title: For online sellers and customer orders
paragraphs: Use consistent product descriptions and record final package measurements. Confirm recipient details before handover, and explain that estimated delivery dates can change. Share the approved tracking link rather than internal paperwork or screenshots containing private customer data.

If a customer needs to return an item, contact operations before dispatching it back. Return acceptance, customs treatment, charges and any original carrier reference need a separate review. The website does not automatically issue return labels or refunds.

sections.title: For pallets and larger movements
paragraphs: Identify whether the cargo is loose, palletised, crated or containerised and whether it can be stacked. Share piece dimensions and weights rather than only a total, and flag lifting or vehicle-access constraints at both ends.

Discuss the proposed service and handling responsibilities with your shipping contact. Warehousing, scheduled collections, customs brokerage, specialist handling and account terms are not automatically included or guaranteed by this page.

sections.title: Keep communication connected to the reference
paragraphs: Once a shipment is confirmed, use its Relay reference when discussing documents, changes or payment questions. Keep a clear internal record of who approved the arrangements and what the quotation covered.

Relay operations creates shipments and publishes milestones. Customers can track without registering an account. There is no customer self-booking, ecommerce platform integration or automated order synchronisation in the current website.

pages.title: Tracking and delivery help
pages.kicker: KNOW THE UPDATE. KNOW THE NEXT STEP.
pages.heading: Make sense of your shipment’s progress.
pages.intro: Tracking is most useful when it is clear about what has been recorded and what still needs confirmation. Here is how to read Relay updates and ask for help.

sections.title: Find the reference and check the latest event
paragraphs: Your sender or Relay shipping contact provides the tracking reference after registration. Enter it on the tracking page or use the private link you were given. Compare the timestamp of the latest published milestone with its location and public note.

Locations are manually recorded by operations. Only approved coordinates appear on the customer map, and connecting lines are not continuous vehicle positions. An empty map does not mean a shipment has not moved.

sections.title: Common milestones, in plain language
items: Booked: a shipment record has been created; this alone does not establish collection.
Picked up / at origin: operations has published the relevant collection or origin-handling milestone.
In transit: a movement update has been recorded; the shipment may pass through additional handling points.
Customs clearance: a customs-related stage has been published; review its note for context.
Out for delivery: a delivery-stage update has been recorded; it is not a guaranteed appointment.
On hold: progress needs attention; check the note and contact your known shipping contact.
Delivered / cancelled: the published record is closed in that status; ask operations about any discrepancy.

sections.title: If an update is late or a delivery detail needs to change
paragraphs: Keep the reference, the latest milestone and the question you need answered together. Ask your sender or shipping contact to clarify a missed estimate, address correction or delivery arrangement. Do not arrange a reroute solely by editing a message in the public quote form.

Changes, missed-delivery arrangements and returns depend on the shipment and any partner rules. This site does not automatically reschedule, redirect, refund or generate a return label. If you believe goods arrived damaged, keep the packaging and photographs and promptly ask your shipping contact about the applicable reporting procedure; no claims deadline is established by this guide.

sections.title: Protect your reference and verify payment requests
paragraphs: Treat a tracking link as private: anyone with it may see the published shipment information, approved images and active payment instructions. Recipient contact details, full addresses and private admin records are not included in public tracking.

Use only the website and contact channel you recognise. If a transfer request is unexpected, confirm it independently with your known shipping contact before paying. Submitting a bank reference does not mark funds as received; an administrator must verify the transfer.
